purpose: Teach: 三国志/ハンマー/バイキング/スターウォーズ/カーニバル/肺炎/領事館/赤ワイン

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが三国志全巻を集められたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young, he collected all the Three Kingdoms books.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gaze slightly distant. Warm but caught in memory. Measured pace, allowing space for the detail to settle. Slight hum of affection on the final phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、日曜大工でハンマーを使われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and didn't you take good care of yourself with that carpentry, dear? Using the hammer and all.
lines.style: Gentle correction wrapped in warmth. Tender, almost singing the words. A small smile in the voice. She's redirecting him back to their shared life, not his parents. Intimate and steady.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、ホテルのバイキング朝食が珍しかったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, a hotel buffet breakfast was quite something special.
lines.style: The same wistful distance, but grounded now in his own youth. Slower still. A quietness that suggests he's remembering the taste of that rarity. Voice carries the weight of seventy years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様とスターウォーズの映画を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And didn't you watch Star Wars with the grandchildren, dear? I remember how much you enjoyed that.
lines.style: Gentle, insistent warmth. She's weaving him back into the present, into the things he did, not just heard about. Voice steady and sure. A little teasing affection underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、ブラジルのカーニバルを羨ましく思われたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was younger, I remember envying Brazil's Carnival—wished I could see it.
lines.style: A longer exhalation before the sentence. Softer, more vulnerable than before. He's reached into a private longing. Voice carries both the old yearning and the acceptance of time. Almost confiding.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年は肺炎にもお気を付けてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You were so careful about your health in those later years, weren't you? Especially with the pneumonia concerns.
lines.style: Tender but more present, less distant. She's honoring his care of himself. Voice carries both gentleness and the quiet weight of knowing his fraility. No performance, just true regard.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが領事館でお仕事された時期もあったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father even had a posting at the consulate for a time.
lines.style: A shift—pride surfaces beneath the wistfulness. He lingers on the word 'consulate.' Voice carries both the memory and a quiet sense of his father's importance. Measured, but with slight emphasis on the detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お祝いに赤ワインを開けられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you'd open a bottle of red wine to celebrate, didn't you? Those quiet celebrations we had.
lines.style: Warmth blooms fully here. Tender and closing. Her voice softens, almost singing the words. She's bringing him home to their life together—the toasts, the simple joy. A gentle fadeout, like settling into memory together.
